LESSON: DIMENSIONING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.2: Dimensioning

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Dimensioning. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is dimensioning applied in drawings?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the types of dimensioning in drawing
2. draw lines used for dimensioning in drawing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DIMENSIONING
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Dimensioning helps you succeed in PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

KEY FACTS: DIMENSIONING
Study Dimensioning like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the types of dimensioning in drawing

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the types of dimensioning in drawing. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the types of dimensioning in drawing.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Safety first: State one safety rule before practising “Dimensioning”.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the types of dimensioning in drawing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Draw lines used for dimensioning in drawing

What this means
In this part you learn to draw lines used for dimensioning in drawing. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: draw lines used for dimensioning in drawing.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Steps: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Dimensioning.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can draw lines used for dimensioning in drawing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Dimensioning is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: State one safety rule before practising “Dimensioning”. (skill: identify the types of dimensioning in drawing)

Example 2: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Dimensioning. (skill: draw lines used for dimensioning in drawing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Dimensioning to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the types of dimensioning in drawing.
3. Practise this skill: draw lines used for dimensioning in drawing.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Dimensioning from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Dimensioning: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Dimensioning?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is dimensioning applied in drawings?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Dimensioning means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the types of dimensioning in drawing.
5. Be able to: draw lines used for dimensioning in drawing.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
